# Twitter Voice Guide

## Audience

Two overlapping audiences:

1. **Anime Twitter** — Gen Z, shitpost energy, reacts to cards and archetype content
2. **Build-in-public Twitter** — indie hackers, AI builders, respond to technical posts

Write for one audience per tweet. Don't try to bridge both in a single post.

## Voice rules

- **Lowercase is fine**. Often better. "dropped my arc and taking damage" hits harder than proper sentence case.
- **First 5 words are everything**. They decide if anyone reads the rest.
- **No hashtags**. Zero. Hashtags are dead on Twitter.
- **0-1 emoji max per tweet**. Usually 0.
- **Brevity wins**. Aim for 80-180 chars, not max 280.
- **No "🚨" "🔥" "🚀"**. These signal marketing copy instantly.
- **No threads unless a thread is genuinely warranted**. Single tweets get better reach. If threading, max 3 tweets for most content.
- **Include the domain (arcforge.me) sparingly** — once every 3-4 posts, not every post.

## Formats that work

### The unhinged quote

> claude just generated an archetype called "The Haunted Archivist" whose power is remembering every embarrassing thing anyone has ever said to them
>
> this is deeply personal attack material

### The rate-this

> dropped my arc, taking damage. be honest
> [card image]

### The prompt engineering war story

> spent 4 hours trying to stop claude from ending every arc with "and then they found their true self"
>
> the fix was adding "the character does not find their true self" to the system prompt
>
> humbling

### The archetype identification

> fallen prodigy arc = texts back in 4-6 business days, knows more than you about one (1) topic, still hasn't recovered from being gifted in 4th grade

### The feature tease

> your arc doesn't end at episode 1.
> [blurred episode 2 screenshot]

### The builder milestone (for build-in-public audience)

> phase 1 of arcforge is live. 17 people have generated their anime arcs so far. phase 2 (weekly episodes) starts this week.
>
> no paid ads. no launch post. just a product that wants to be shared.
>
> arcforge.me

## Avoid

- Corporate announcement voice: "Excited to announce that..."
- Hustle hook: "3 things I learned building..."
- Fake urgency: "ONLY TODAY"
- Questions that sound like ads: "Ever wondered what your anime arc would be?"
- Emoji strings: "🔥🚀💯"
- Screenshot-of-tweet tweets (too meta)

## Example bank — what good looks like

1. `"neighborhood loner with recursive insight as a power" is diagnostically accurate, claude, thanks`

2. `fallen prodigy arc couples listen to mitski and pretend they don't. pass it on.`

3. `the arc card is the product. everything else is engineering in support of "will a 19 year old screenshot this and post it."`

4. `rate limiting via IP alone: cute. users are on shared wifi. back to the drawing board.`

5. `new archetype just dropped: "The Feral Genius." too online. too weird. somehow always right. we all know one.`

6. `1 week into phase 2 build. the cron job that drops weekly episodes is terrifying me. what if it fires twice. what if it fires zero. what if it fires but claude is down.`

7. `if your arc card isn't something you'd screenshot, you haven't designed it yet. you've just styled a div.`

8. `got an arc back that said my rival is "the polished clone" and i have not recovered`

## Example bank — what BAD looks like (avoid)

1. ❌ `🚀 Excited to announce ArcForge! Generate your personalized anime character arc with AI ✨ Try it now 👇 arcforge.me #AI #Anime #GenZ`
   — Emoji spam, hashtags, "Excited to announce," shameless CTA.

2. ❌ `Have you ever wondered what your anime arc would be? 🤔 Our AI creates a personalized story just for you! ➡️ arcforge.me`
   — Ad-copy question, promotional tone, arrow emoji.

3. ❌ `10 reasons you need to generate your ArcForge arc today: 1. Personalized 2. Unique 3. Shareable...`
   — Listicle, generic benefit-speak.

4. ❌ `i chose a Next.js monolith on purpose. not because i don't know microservices. because pre-PMF infra complexity is usually fear wearing a senior-engineer costume.`
   — The "fear wearing a senior-engineer costume" metaphor is trying too hard to be quotable. Indie/dev Twitter voice is plainer than this. If a phrase feels like it's auditioning for retweets, cut it. Rewrite as flatter observation.

5. ❌ `the arc card is my love letter to everyone who ever felt like a side character in their own life.`
   — Over-written, emotionally performative. ArcForge voice is dry and specific, not earnest and poetic. No love-letter energy. No "everyone who ever felt like X" framings.
